description: The plot illustrates next-token prediction accuracy as a function of training step for two experiments, shown as two line series. The x-axis is labeled “Step,” uses a linear scale, and spans from 0 to 60,000 with regularly spaced tick labels every 10,000. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy (Next Token Prediction),” uses a linear scale, and shows values roughly from 0.10 up to about 0.42 with tick labels at approximately 0.05 intervals (e.g., 0.10, 0.15, …, 0.40). The “Ex1 Accuracy” series is a blue solid line with circular markers; it starts near 0.09 at step 0, rises to about 0.24 at 1,500 steps, increases to about 0.39 at 7,500 steps, and then gradually increases and flattens, reaching about 0.40 at 13,000 steps and about 0.41 by 60,000 steps. The “Ex2 Accuracy” series is a teal solid line with circular markers; it starts near 0.09 at step 0, increases to about 0.27 at 1,500 steps, rises to about 0.28 at 7,500 steps and about 0.29 at 13,000 steps, then increases to about 0.36 at 19,000 steps and continues a gradual rise, reaching about 0.38 around 30,000 steps and about 0.39 by 60,000 steps.
